issues.title: Task-required $(./b4w.ps1) invocation format is broken in bash

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
In Git Bash, run: $(./b4w.ps1) help
Result: "b4w: command not found"

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The help output should display, or the task instructions should use a working invocation method.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The command fails because $(...) is bash command substitution — it runs ./b4w.ps1, captures stdout, then tries to execute that output as a command. SKILL.md line 27 explicitly warns about this, yet the task instructions mandate the broken format.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The task template uses $(./b4w.ps1) syntax which is command substitution in bash. While SKILL.md documents this as a known issue, the task instructions themselves prescribe the broken format. This creates a contradiction where following the task instructions leads to immediate failure, and following the documentation requires deviating from the task instructions.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Update task templates to use ./b4w.sh <command> (bash) or ./b4w.ps1 <command> (PowerShell) instead of $(./b4w.ps1)
- Add a wrapper script or alias that makes the $(...) format work, e.g., a shell function that passes arguments through
- Add a first-run check in the task harness that detects bash and prints a clear migration message

issues.title: JSON values with commas/spaces cannot be set via b4w.sh wrapper

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
./b4w.sh localstorage-set user_prefs '{"lang":"en","tz":"UTC"}'
Result: "Error: error: too many arguments: expected 2, received 3"

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The JSON string should be treated as a single value argument.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The CLI reports "too many arguments" because the JSON value containing commas and spaces is split into multiple arguments by the time it reaches the argument parser. The b4w.sh wrapper's quoting mechanism (line 45-48) does not sufficiently protect against PowerShell's argument parsing when the value contains double-quote characters.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The b4w.sh wrapper escapes double quotes within arguments as \" (line 47) and wraps each argument in double quotes. When PowerShell receives the resulting string, the embedded escaped quotes interact with PowerShell's own parsing, causing the value to be split. The direct pwsh invocation `pwsh -Command "& './b4w.ps1' localstorage-set user_prefs '{\"lang\":\"en\",\"tz\":\"UTC\"}'"` works correctly, suggesting the issue is specifically in the b4w.sh argument transformation pipeline.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: b4w.sh:45-48 (argument escaping loop)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add a --value-base64 flag to storage set commands for safe binary/JSON values
- Add a --file flag to read the value from a file, avoiding shell quoting entirely
- Document the pwsh workaround explicitly in the storage-state.md reference
- Fix the b4w.sh argument quoting to handle embedded double-quotes in PowerShell -Command strings

issues.title: state-save does not include sessionStorage despite 'complete browser state' description

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Set a sessionStorage item, run state-save, clear sessionStorage, run state-load — sessionStorage is not restored.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The help text says state-save saves 'cookies and localStorage'. The task instructions say to save 'complete browser state'. SessionStorage is excluded, which is understandable (it's session-scoped) but the mismatch between task description and actual behavior creates confusion.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: state-save only persists cookies and localStorage. sessionStorage is not included in the saved state file.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: SessionStorage is intentionally scoped to the browsing session and is not typically persisted across sessions. However, the CLI help text ('Save cookies and localStorage to a JSON file') and the task instructions ('save the complete browser state') use inconsistent language that could mislead users into expecting sessionStorage preservation.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Update state-save help text to clarify: 'Save cookies and localStorage to a JSON file (sessionStorage is not persisted)'
- Consider adding state-save --include-session-storage flag for completeness
- Update task instructions to say 'browser storage state' rather than 'complete browser state'

issues.title: Storage command help output lacks usage examples

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run ./b4w.sh cookie-set --help — it shows options but no examples.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The --help output for storage commands should include at least one usage example showing common flag combinations, similar to how the storage-state.md reference doc provides examples.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: cookie-set --help only shows: Arguments: <name>, <value>; Options: --domain, --path, --expires, --httpOnly, --secure, --sameSite. No examples of how to combine these flags.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The CLI help system provides argument/option reference but not usage examples. The storage-state.md reference doc fills this gap, but users who only use --help won't discover the patterns. This is a consistent pattern across all storage commands.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add a one-line example to each storage command's --help output (e.g., 'Example: cookie-set session abc123 --domain .example.com --path / --httpOnly --secure')
- Add a reference pointer in --help: 'See skills/browser4-cli/references/storage-state.md for more examples'

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
./b4w.sh localstorage-clear
Output: "localStorage cleared: 0 entrie(s)."
./b4w.sh sessionstorage-clear
Output: "sessionStorage cleared: 0 entrie(s)."

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: "localStorage cleared: 0 entries." or "localStorage cleared: 0 entry/entries."

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The word "entrie(s)" is a misspelling — it should be "entries" or "entry/entries".

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: Likely a typo in the CLI output formatting code for the clear commands. The '(s)' parenthetical pluralization pattern is used, but the base word is misspelled as 'entrie' instead of 'entry'.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body: - Change "entrie(s)" to "entries" or "entry/entries" in the clear-command output strings

issues.title: cookie-list has no --name filter — must use separate cookie-get command

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
./b4w.sh cookie-list --help
Only shows --domain and --path filters. No --name option.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Users might expect `cookie-list --name session_id` to filter by name, similar to --domain and --path.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: cookie-list only filters by domain and path. Finding a specific cookie by name requires the separate cookie-get command.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The cookie-list command was designed with domain/path filtering (browser-centric) but without name filtering. This is a design choice — cookie-get serves the single-cookie use case — but it's not immediately obvious to new users.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add a --name filter to cookie-list for consistency with --domain and --path
- Or: document the distinction clearly in --help output ("Use cookie-get <name> to look up a specific cookie")

issues.title: No --json flag support on cookie-list despite JSON being the default output

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./b4w.sh cookie-list --help — no --json option listed. ./b4w.sh --json cookie-list — works but not discoverable from command help.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The --json flag should be listed in per-command --help if the command supports it, or the default JSON output behavior should be documented.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: cookie-list outputs JSON by default, but --help doesn't mention this or the --json flag. Users might not realize they can pipe the output to jq or other JSON tools.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: cookie-list always outputs JSON (it's the default format), so --json may be treated as redundant. However, the SKILL.md describes --json as a general output mode flag, and its absence from per-command help reduces discoverability.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add --json to the options list in cookie-list --help with a note that JSON is the default output format
- Alternatively, add a note at the top: 'Output is always JSON'

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run ./b4w.sh cookie-set test val without --domain — where is the cookie scoped?

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The default domain behavior should be documented in --help or storage-state.md.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: When --domain is omitted, the cookie is likely set for the current page's domain, but this is not documented. Users must either know CDP cookie behavior or experiment.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The CLI delegates to CDP's Network.setCookie which defaults to the current page's domain. This implicit behavior is not surfaced in the CLI documentation.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Document the default domain behavior in cookie-set --help: 'Defaults to the current page domain if omitted'
- Add the same note to storage-state.md
